summary: OpenTelemetry gauges in the matching service leak metric entries indefinitely because the gaugeAdapter stores label combinations in a map that only adds entries and never removes them, causing unbounded Prometheus metric cardinality growth over pod lifetime.
userImpact: Long-lived Temporal clusters with many task queues and worker build IDs see unbounded metric cardinality growth, increasing Prometheus scrape overhead and resource usage on matching pods.
rootCause: The gaugeAdapter.values map in common/metrics/otel_metrics_handler.go stores gauge entries keyed by label sets but only adds entries and never removes them, so metrics from unloaded physical task queues persist indefinitely.
proposedFix: Explicitly evict metric entries when a task queue is unloaded from the matching service.
workaround: Use the excludeTags field in the Temporal service config to exclude high-cardinality labels like workflow_type, task_queue, or build_id from metrics.
keyQuote: Gauge values leak in `gaugeAdapter.values` — entries are never removed
